subject: System Design
title: The Nasdaq Facebook IPO Glitch
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Nasdaq Facebook IPO Glitch.

hook.text: On May 18, 2012, Facebook's IPO was the most anticipated stock launch in history. Nasdaq couldn't handle it.

buildup.text: A flood of orders overwhelmed Nasdaq's system. The opening was delayed 30 minutes.

discovery.text: A race condition in Nasdaq's matching engine caused orders to be lost or duplicated.

twist.text: Traders didn't know if their orders had been executed. Some accidentally bought twice the shares they wanted.

climax.text: Nasdaq paid $10 million in fines and $62 million to affected firms. A race condition in the busiest IPO ever.

punchline.text: A race condition ruined the biggest IPO in history.

quiz.question: What bug caused the Nasdaq Facebook IPO failure?
options: A race condition in the order matching engine
